analysis: The production change in LaunchAgent.swift is small. At head lines 268-269 the doc comment documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES. At head line 289, DeadlineAdmissionFixes.environmentKey is added to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys, which feeds passthroughEnvKeys (lines 298-311) and passthroughEnvironment (lines 325-346). This persists a non-empty operator-set value from the installing shell into the launchd plist's EnvironmentVariables. It uses the same allowlist mechanism as the neighbouring keys (PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE and others). It is a static key allowlist that forwards only non-empty values, so no new trust boundary is crossed. The surrounding worker opt-in handling is unchanged: only AppAttestWorkerSelection.qualificationEnvironment="1" is forwarded, and no diagnostic or fault flags. The kill switch's semantics are inferred from the test (default-on, explicit off disables). The change affects only deadline-admission estimator behavior, which is a performance and availability control, not an authorization, attestation, encryption or billing control. Base and head are otherwise identical across the supplied text. That covers the stop/disable lifecycle, kickstart, the bootstrap path and plist atomic write; none changed. The related threat entries are T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-003, and neither is touched. The only new file, AdmissionRateEstimatorTests.swift, is test-only. Its patch excerpt is truncated and the unit has no text. I saw only the first ~40 lines, which are synthetic scripted-engine tests with no production impact. Remaining unverified: the DeadlineAdmissionFixes implementation and the EngineV2Bridge admissionFixes plumbing are not in the supplied batch. I cannot confirm that a disabled or malformed value fails safe, or that an operator cannot widen admission to starve other requests. In the threat model that would be a DoS concern only for the provider's own operator, who is already the trust owner, so I see no regression.
